messages:
joel: small UX bug I bumped into when saving a per-route view as a shared saved query. The "pinned model" pill stays visible in the console but when another user runs it the quota preview shows totals for ALL models.

anya: ah interesting. so savedquery serialization includes the pinned model id, but the server-side preview ignores it?

sam: server currently expands savedquery filters to normalized routing policies before computing quota estimates. That normalization step flattens single-model pins into the route's default model list.

joel: repro steps: open route C -> pin model m12 -> save view "team-c-m12" -> share to group. Another user opens the saved query and sees preview cost = route-total tokens (x10) instead of just m12 tokens.

kevin: is this a telemetry issue too? We might be attributing cost under a different model in billing traces.

sam: good call. Our billing events derive the model_id from the routing policy snapshot that runs at execution time, not from the savedquery payload. If the policy later changes, cost attribution drifts.

anya: two separate problems: (1) UX mismatch in preview, (2) long-term attribution/consistency for saved queries. Proposals: A) persist an explicit pinned_model field in the savedquery resource that the preview and executor both honor, B) keep current behavior but show a clear warning that preview uses current routing policies, or C) freeze routing policy snapshot at save time.

joel: I prefer A for clarity and minimum surprise. C feels heavy (policy freeze rollback complications). B is lowest effort but still confusing.

kevin: For billing we probably want a hybrid: persist pinned_model for user-facing attribution and emit a policy_version tag so infra can reconcile when policies change. That lets us show historical context.

sam: implementation notes: savedquery resource currently looks like: 
```
{ name, route_id, filters: [...], metadata: {...} }
```
We can add "pinned_model_id" and "policy_snapshot_id" fields. Backwards compatible: if pinned_model_id exists, preview uses it; otherwise fallback to route policy.

anya: also need to update the console SDK to surface pinned_model in the share dialog and in the preview modal. UX copy: "This saved view will always target model m12 unless routing policy overrides are explicitly requested." (maybe too techy).

joel: shorter: "Targets model m12 unless you choose a different model on run."

ops-bot: incident note: billing-team flagged one support ticket where customer disputed cost from shared savedviews (ticket #4287).

kevin: timeline? We should ship server-side schema change + migration that defaults pinned_model_id=null (no break). Client changes behind flag. Then GA in 2 sprints.

sam: will add unit tests: (1) preview respects pinned_model, (2) executor tags events with policy_snapshot_id and model_id, (3) migration idempotent. Also add e2e: save with pinned model -> another user previews -> assert preview cost matches pinned model sample.

anya: UX nit: when a saved query with pinned_model is opened by a user who doesn't have permission to use that model (entitlement), show a soft error: "This saved view references a model you can't run. Click to choose an alternative."

joel: good call. Add telemetry event for "savedquery.pinned_model.unavailable" so support can trace.

kevin: I'll coordinate with billing to ensure policy_snapshot_id is included in cost export so disputes can be traced back.

joel: great. I'll draft the product ticket and include mockups for the share modal and preview badge. Thanks folks.
